summary_responses.response: The National Credit Union Administration issued a final rule under 12 CFR Part 701 (RIN 3133-AF93), effective January 4, 2027, amending its criteria for determining associational common bonds. The rule clarifies that requiring members to purchase a good, product, or service from a group as a condition of membership will no longer automatically disqualify the group from eligibility as a recognized association. Adopting the April 8, 2026 proposal with modifications, the Board responded to 18 public comments received by June 8, 2026, most of which supported the change. The amendments detail how NCUA evaluates client-customer relationships, provide relevant examples, and simplify its review process for pre-approved groups. The long-standing policy that associations based primarily on a client-customer relationship do not qualify remains intact, and the rule applies only to single associational and multiple common bond federal credit unions.
